title: Adopt react-hooks 7's React Compiler rules deliberately, with the three faults they already found
goal: eslint-plugin-react-hooks 7 expands configs.recommended from two rules to sixteen at error severity. ITEM-1 replaced the spread with one named rule rather than adopt thirteen blocking rules as a side effect of a peer-dependency bump. This adopts them on purpose, starting with set-state-in-effect, and fixes the three real faults they found. Nothing currently guards ITEM-1's use-media-query fix: no test can, because it preserved behaviour, and the rule that caught it is one of these.
acceptance: Given eslint.config.js, when lint runs, then react-hooks/set-state-in-effect is enabled and apps/web/src/ui/use-media-query.ts fails if its setState-in-effect shape returns

Given apps/web/src/features/quick-add/quick-add.tsx, when lint runs, then its reset-on-open no longer calls setState inside an effect, and Quick Add still starts empty every time it opens so nothing is recorded twice
Given apps/web/src/features/plan/plan-screen.tsx, when lint runs, then react-hooks/preserve-manual-memoization passes and the React Compiler no longer skips optimising the component
Given each rule newly enabled, when it is first relied on, then it has been seen failing once on purpose (TEST-09)

reviews.summary: Pass, nothing open. CODE-16 is the item: a key is React's documented way to reset state when a prop changes, and setState in an effect is what its own rule forbids. MONEY-08 is the one with consequences — the hazard is recording the same amount twice, and a remount makes that impossible for all state rather than the four an effect listed. Proven by removing the key and watching only that test fail.

Pass, nothing open. The rule worth checking was DES-10: a remount could have broken focus on open, and it demonstrably does not — the amount field still holds focus, asserted by a test reading document.activeElement. DES-13 computed from the tokens rather than deferred: all twelve text pairs clear 4.5:1, worst 5.75:1, focus ring clears 3:1 at 8:1.

Pass, nothing open. Nothing visual changes: no colour, token, spacing, radius or size appears in the diff, and no element is added — the change removes an effect and a memo. DES-13 computed from the tokens rather than deferred, all twelve text pairs clearing 4.5:1. DES-06 holds: the only danger use in scope is Plan's over-allocation, which is money going wrong.

Pass, nothing open. No serious problem and no boundary moves: validation and parsing stay in core untouched, and the only value introduced is an integer counter inside app-shell. PRIV-01 is marginally stronger — a draft holding an amount is destroyed with the component on close rather than overwritten later, so a previous opening's figure does not sit behind a closed sheet.

Pass. All four criteria hold and each was demonstrated by breaking something first: 16 rules in the computed config with set-state-in-effect at error, the old use-media-query shape now raising that error, and removing app-shell's key failing the money-safety test and only that one. The refactor needed no test edited, which is itself evidence the tests check behaviour.
